items.title: PM Anwar attends Citrawarna 2026 launch and cultural parade
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim attended the opening ceremony and parade of Citrawarna 2026 at Dataran Merdeka yesterday, a flagship Tourism Malaysia event held as part of the Visit Malaysia 2026 (VM2026) campaign. He was joined by Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing, Deputy Minister Chiew Choon Man, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Tourism Malaysia director-general Mohd Amirul Rizal Abdul Rahim. Supported by Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL), Warisan Kuala Lumpur, the National Department for Culture and Arts (JKKN), Istana Budaya and the National Textile Museum, Citrawarna 2026 aims to promote Malaysia’s arts, culture and heritage tourism to domestic and international visitors.

items.title: Police detain man for assaulting Ipoh officer issuing compound notice
items.summary: IPOH, July 26 — Police have detained a man to assist investigations into an incident in which an Ipoh City Council enforcement officer was assaulted and threatened while issuing a compound notice at Jalan Pengkalan Barat 35 yesterday. Ipoh district police chief ACP Muhammad Najib Hamzah said the 42-year-old suspect allegedly acted aggressively by trying to hit the officer with a vehicle, tailing him, pulling his shirt collar and making threats. “Acting on information, a team of officers from the Ipoh District Police Headquarters Criminal Investigation Department detained the suspect today at about 12.40 pm to assist investigations.

items.title: Raja Muda Of Selangor, wife, welcome first child, Tengku Alia Amira
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, July 26 — The Raja Muda of Selangor, Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah and his wife Datin Paduka Seri Afzaa Fadini Abdul Aziz yesterday announced the birth of their first child, Tengku Alia Amira Tengku Amir Shah. Tengku Amir Shah and Datin Paduka Seri Afzaa Fadini were married in a royal solemnisation ceremony at Masjid Istana Diraja, Istana Alam Shah, Klang, on Oct 2, 2025. The royal couple was solemnised by Selangor Mufti Datuk Dr Anhar Opir, witnessed by Tengku Panglima Raja Selangor Tengku Ahmad Shah Alhaj and Tengku Indera Pahlawan Diraja Tengku Datuk Setia Putra Alhaj in the private wedding ceremony.

items.title: BN chairman defends manifesto as original and improved, dismisses ‘copying’ accusations
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, July 26 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has rejected allegations that BN’s manifesto, launched yesterday, was copied from those of other parties. The Umno president said the manifesto built on BN’s existing agenda and had been refined to meet current requirements. Early voting for the Negeri Sembilan state polls will take place this Tuesday, with polling day scheduled for Aug 1.

items.title: Third flood relief centre opens in Melaka as number of evacuees rises
items.summary: MELAKA, July 26 — The third temporary relief centre has been opened in Melaka to accommodate the increasing number of flood victims as of 8 pm yesterday. The Melaka State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said the third relief centre opened is at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Bukit Tembakau at 3.15pm yesterday. Three areas in Jasin are affected, namely Kampung Pulai, Kampung Serkam and Kampung Bukit Tembakau.

items.title: PM Anwar demands swift action on Felda initiatives amid settler frustration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants the seven initiatives announced earlier to help Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) settlers implemented without further delay. Anwar said he has requested progress reports on all initiatives, which include assistance to Felda and new generation housing, to be provided every month so that their implementation is not delayed. On July 7, the Prime Minister announced seven initiatives in conjunction with Felda Settlers’ Day and 70th Anniversary celebration, including strengthening digital literacy for settlers involving an allocation of RM15.85 million to 317 eligible Felda schemes.

items.title: Malaysians in Qatar urged to follow security advisories, avoid military areas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Malaysians in Qatar have been advised to follow security instructions issued by the local authorities and avoid military areas following the latest developments in the Gulf region. The Embassy of Malaysia in Doha also urged Malaysians to remain vigilant, stay alert to their surroundings, and avoid being influenced by or spreading false information and rumours. The embassy also advised Malaysians to check the latest flight schedules before travelling from Qatar and to ensure their personal and family information are kept up to date.

items.title: Perikatan launches Negeri Sembilan election manifesto with six main pillars
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 26 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) today launched its manifesto outlining six main pillars for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election. The manifesto, with the theme ‘PN Sepakat Hebatkan Negeri Sembilan’, was launched by PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar. For the latest updates on the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election, visit https://prn.bernama.com/n9.

items.title: One killed, 15 wounded as car hits crowd near Berlin Gay Pride
items.summary: BERLIN: At least one person was killed and around 15 wounded after a car hit the crowd on the outskirts of the Berlin Gay Pride parade, police said Saturday. "A vehicle entered the Tiergarten park and hit several people and injured them" just before 10pm (2000 GMT), police posted on social media, later adding that they were hunting for the occupants of the car. The Gay Pride event was cut short and police told participants to "Go home, please" and sealed off the area where the people were injured.

items.title: Parents divided over merit system for students who report bullying, drugs [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Parents are divided over a proposal to introduce a merit system for students who report bullying, extortion or drug involvement in schools, raising concerns that their children could later be targeted. Parent Action Group for Education Malaysia (Page) chairman Datin Noor Azimah Abdul Rahim said while there were concerns about violence in schools, parents were also worried about how their children would be protected when they report crimes. He said it would help school authorities detect misconduct early while cultivating a strong culture of reporting among students.

items.title: Lessons from Iran: Malaysia must shape nuclear narrative early
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: As tensions between Iran and the United States continue to affect the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global energy shipping lane, the crisis has reminded many countries, including Malaysia, that a nuclear programme is never judged on local and technical grounds alone. Dr Habibreza Arzani, cultural counsellor at Iran's embassy in Kuala Lumpur, said Iran's experience showed that nuclear development was often judged not only on technical grounds, but also through the political narratives built around a country's scientific advancement. He said Malaysia should invest early in public diplomacy, legal transparency and international communication before any civilian nuclear programme could be framed negatively by outside actors.

items.title: Clock ticking on Malaysia's nuclear future, says industry veteran
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia risks falling behind other countries if it continues to delay a decision on nuclear power, said veteran nuclear industry figure Raja Datuk Abdul Aziz Raja Adnan. The former Atomic Energy Licensing Board director-general said the issue was no longer whether Malaysia had studied nuclear energy, but whether it had the political will to act on years of technical groundwork. "We are not the only country looking at nuclear energy.

items.title: Syria bus crash kills at least 35
items.summary: DAMASCUS: A crash between two passenger buses in a central-eastern desert region of Syria on Saturday killed at least 35 people, state media said. News agency SANA, quoting a health ministry official, also said 30 others were injured in the "collision between two passenger buses on the Damascus-Deir Ezzor road." The interior ministry said the crash was between "a bus carrying a number of internal security forces personnel and a civilian bus", without specifying how many of the casualties were from its forces.

items.title: Groups warn against nuclear rush
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must not rush into nuclear power without first answering hard questions on cost, safety, radioactive waste, foreign dependency and public accountability, consumer and environmental groups said. "Nuclear energy is not merely an electricity generation project. But it would be misleading to conclude that nuclear energy would automatically lower electricity bills or reduce government spending on energy subsidies, he said.

items.title: Hormuz tensions reignite Malaysia's nuclear energy debate
items.summary: Malaysian Nuclear Agency director-general Dr Muhammad Rawi Mohamed Zin said the geopolitical uncertainty had disrupted global oil and gas supply chains, affecting Malaysia's energy security. He said nuclear power offered a more resilient option as nuclear fuel did not require frequent shipments compared with fossil fuels. Dr Rawi said Malaysia's energy debate should not be limited to whether nuclear power would immediately lower electricity tariffs.

items.title: Tunisia's Sidi Bou Said inscribed on UNESCO World Heritage list
items.summary: TUNIS: Tunisia's coastal city of Sidi Bou Said, famed for its blue and white houses, has been inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage List, the organisation said Saturday. "New inscription on the UNESCO World Heritage List: Village of Sidi Bou Saïd," the UN organisation said in a social media post, following a meeting of its committee in South Korea. The village was built in the 18th century around the shrine of the Sufi master Sidi Bou Said.

items.title: Once a DAP stronghold, Chennah now a key battleground [WATCH]
items.summary: SEREMBAN: On paper, Chennah appears to be one of DAP's safest seats in Negri Sembilan. DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke has held the seat comfortably since 2013, transforming what was once an MCA strong-hold into a Pakatan Harapan fortress. Loke enters the race with significant advantages.

items.title: Kazakh leader tells Putin war should end, Ukraine launches fresh strikes
items.summary: In occupied Ukraine, Russian-installed authorities said a Ukrainian strike had killed 12 people at a seaside "tourist camp", as well as one more in a Moscow-held town and two in Russian border villages. Kyiv said Russian attacks had killed five people in eastern and southern Ukraine, and two crew members were missing after a Russian strike on a cargo ship carrying corn. Moscow said Ukraine – which has intensified its retaliatory strikes – launched more than 300 drones into Russia Saturday, including on far-flung regions.

items.title: For nearly a century, this Penang family in Jelutong has let the sun make its soy sauce
items.summary: Today, brothers Kam Kam Yoon, 87, and Kam Pak Yuen continue running San Kwan Loong Soy Sauce Factory using the same natural fermentation method their mother brought from China when the family business was established almost 100 years ago. “We still make our soy sauce using natural fermentation under the sun,” he said. Kam Kam Yoon took over the San Kwan Loong soy sauce factory business at 19 years old.

items.title: Wildfires send nearly 260,000 fleeing in France and Spain
items.summary: BORDEAUX: Unchecked wildfires raging Saturday in France's southwest and near Spain's capital Madrid have forced nearly 260,000 people to flee and prompted Paris to deploy its military. France initially hustled 197,000 people from areas around popular vacation spot Bordeaux – one of its biggest-ever peacetime evacuations, though 3,000 were later allowed to return. In Spain, where 60,000 people were evacuated from villages west of Madrid, Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said the priority was "to save lives" as he visited the fire zone.

items.title: PN launches six-pillar manifesto for Negri Sembilan election
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Perikatan Nasional yesterday launched its manifesto outlining six main pillars for the Negri Sembilan election. Themed "PN Sepakat Hebatkan Negri Sembilan", the manifesto was launched by PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar. Early voting for the Negri Sembilan election will take place this Tuesday (July 28), with polling day scheduled for Aug 1.

items.title: Sanusi's statement cannot be taken lightly - Azalina
items.summary: Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said such rhetoric creates the impression that Malaysians of Chinese and Indian descent have another homeland, while suggesting that only Malays truly belong to Malaysia. Malaysia is their homeland. The same Constitution also guarantees the legitimate rights and status of every citizen regardless of their ancestry," she said in a statement today.

items.title: Negri Sembilan polls: BN manifesto not copied from PH, says Zahid
items.summary: PORT DICKSON: Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said there was no basis to claim that Barisan Nasional had copied or "copy-pasted" the Pakatan Harapan manifesto for the Negri Sembilan election. He said the substance of BN's manifesto was not new, but rather the result of the party's continuous efforts over many years. Zahid also warned BN's rivals against making baseless accusations merely to gain political mileage.

items.title: PM attends Citrawarna 2026 as Malaysia showcases cultural diversity to global visitors
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim launched the annual cultural showcase at Dataran Merdeka, with the three-day event featuring 3,500 performers representing states, three federal territories and the nation's multicultural communities in its signature Colours of Parade (Citra Perarakan). Also present was Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing. Citrawarna 2026 features four signature experiences: Colours of Parade, Colours of Flavour, Colours of Culture and Colours of Art.

items.title: Fear, arrests keep Cambodians quiet decade after critic's murder
items.summary: UNION leader Chhim Sithar served two years in prison after going up against the Cambodian government. Cambodia has four times as many political prisoners today as compared to 2016, the year Kem Ley was shot dead in a Phnom Penh cafe. Cambodia's main opposition party was banned and its leader Kem Sokha jailed the year after Kem Ley was killed, while several independent media outlets have since been shuttered.

items.title: The tarnished legacy of fired forensic ICC prosecutor Karim Khan
items.summary: KARIM Khan will go down in the history of the International Criminal Court (ICC) as the prosecutor who clinched arrest warrants against the leaders of Russia and Israel, but also as the one who "poisoned the atmosphere" in the institution. But the forensic spotlight shifted to Khan himself after a female staffer accused him of sexual assault — allegations he strongly denies — ultimately costing him his job at the ICC. At his swearing-in ceremony in 2021 as chief prosecutor of the Hague-based court, Khan said the ICC should be judged on its actions: "The proof of the pudding should be in the eating."

items.title: Tengku Amir Shah, wife welcome baby girl
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Raja Muda of Selangor, Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah and his wife Datin Paduka Seri Afzaa Fadini Abdul Aziz today announced the birth of their first child, Tengku Alia Amira Tengku Amir Shah. Tengku Amir Shah and Datin Paduka Seri Afzaa Fadini were married in a royal solemnisation ceremony at Masjid Istana Diraja, Istana Alam Shah, Klang, on Oct 2, 2025. The royal couple was solemnised by Selangor Mufti Datuk Dr Anhar Opir, witnessed by Tengku Panglima Raja Selangor Tengku Ahmad Shah Alhaj and Tengku Indera Pahlawan Diraja Tengku Datuk Setia Putra Alhaj in the private wedding ceremony.

items.title: Sonam Wangchuk: 59-year-old who rallied India's Gen Z against Modi and won
items.summary: INDIAN social activist Sonam Wangchuk may be pushing 60, but he was one of the faces of a "Cockroach" Gen Z movement that managed to oust Prime Minister Narendra Modi's education minister over exam paper leaks, having fasted for 26 days. Wangchuk, who is widely believed to have inspired the lead character in a Bollywood blockbuster, is best known for campaigning on issues affecting his Himalayan region of Ladakh, bordering China. That helped turn the issue into a broader Gen Z movement, piling pressure on Modi and leading on Saturday to the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

items.title: Man held for allegedly assaulting, threatening Ipoh City Council enforcement officer
items.summary: IPOH: A 42-year-old man has been arrested for allegedly assaulting and threatening an Ipoh City Council (MBI) enforcement officer while the latter was issuing a compound notice in Pengkalan here yesterday. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Muhammad Najib Hamzah said the man was detained about 12.40pm today. He said the incident occurred at Jalan Pengkalan Barat 35 when the enforcement officer was carrying out his duties.

items.title: NST Leader: How syndicates became global enterprises
items.summary: FOR those who have been wondering why organised crime syndicates are ubiquitous, the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) has an answer. According to a new report by the UNODC released in Bangkok on Tuesday, once locally rooted syndicates have merged into a single transnational, tech-driven criminal economy sophisticated enough to outpace conventional law enforcement. Transnational Crime Inc is perhaps the best way to capture the explosive growth of Southeast Asian organised crime syndicates spreading their tentacles, corporate-like, globally.

items.title: Modi's education minister quits as Indian youth protesters claim victory, end protest
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian youth protesters called off weeks of demonstrations and celebrated in the streets on Saturday after the education minister quit and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government bowed to demands including calls to fix a cheating-prone exam system. The worst political crisis of Modi's third term in office had peaked this week when thousands of protesters marched on parliament, with police using tear gas to control them. Modi's party faces key state elections next year.

items.title: Malaysians in Qatar urged to follow security advisories, avoid military areas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians in Qatar have been advised to follow security instructions issued by the local authorities and avoid military areas following the latest developments in the Gulf region. The Embassy of Malaysia in Doha also urged Malaysians to remain vigilant, stay alert to their surroundings, and avoid being influenced by or spreading false information and rumours. The embassy also advised Malaysians to check the latest flight schedules before travelling from Qatar and to ensure their personal and family information are kept up to date.

items.title: Illegally parked vehicles disrupt buses, Rapid KL identifies hotspots
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Rapid KL is working with authorities to identify locations frequently affected by traffic obstructions caused by illegally parked vehicles. This was following an incident that disrupted bus operations along Jalan Ampang. A viral video shows a Rapid KL bus on Route 300 (Maluri Depot–Lebuh Ampang) struggling to continue its journey from Jalan Yap Kwan Seng to Jalan Ampang.

items.title: Anwar wants Felda initiatives implemented soon, demands monthly progress reports
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants seven previously announced initiatives to assist Felda settlers to be implemented soon. Anwar said he wanted monthly progress reports on all the projects to prevent delays. He said the government would establish a dedicated committee to resolve long-standing issues involving second-generation Felda settlers.

items.title: Push to unveil Tabung Haji RCI report grows
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Experts have called for the immediate release of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), saying it is necessary to establish the truth, protect depositors and improve the institution's governance. While supporting greater transparency, senior lecturer in political science at Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) in Seremban, Dr Mazlan Che Soh, said the report should not become a tool for assigning blame before legal proceedings are completed or for pursuing short-term political interests. While acknowledging that the report's release could influence the views of some voters, particularly Malay-Muslim voters and TH depositors, Mazlan said it would not necessarily lead to a significant shift in overall public support.

items.title: BN will 'call the shots' in understanding with PN, says Tok Mat
items.summary: He said BN would remain the dominant partner and "call the shots" if entrusted to form the Negri Sembilan government, likening the coalition to a company where the majority shareholder determines its direction. Mohamad said concerns would only be justified if BN were the minority partner. he said.

items.title: Negri Sembilan polls: BN-PN pact should remain electoral understanding, says Tok Mat
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Barisan Nasional's pact with Perikatan Nasional in Negri Sembilan should remain an electoral understanding rather than be turned into a formal coalition, said Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. The BN deputy chairman said if the understanding proved to be a workable formula, there would be no need to change it. "We have reached an understanding first and should move one step at a time.

items.title: Three secondary school students in Ampang detained over bullying incident
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Police have arrested three male secondary school students near here on suspicion of beating another student at a block of flats in Ampang. Ampang Jaya District Police Chief ACP Khairul Anuar Khalid said that during the incident at 12.31 pm yesterday, the victim was taken to the bottom of a staircase at a block in Flat Sri Nilam, Ampang, by a male student before being struck on the face and body by the suspects. Earlier, a 3-minute and 29-second video showing a male student being beaten by another student went viral on social media, having been filmed by a third individual.

items.title: Autistic girl dies in 13th-floor apartment fall in Kuala Terengganu
items.summary: Kuala Terengganu police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the department received a call around 7.50 am reporting a young girl lying in the sixth-floor parking area, believed to have fallen from a 13th-floor window. “The victim was pronounced dead at the scene by a medical officer from Hospital Sultanah Nur Zahirah (HSNZ),” he said in a statement today. He said the victim’s mother realised her daughter was missing only after another resident informed her at around 7am.

items.title: Anwar says there is a need to reconstruct history to the Malaysian narrative
items.summary: He said history must not be dictated by the country’s former colonial masters, whether it is the United Kingdom, Japan or the United States. “It must be determined by our people and reconstructed to give meaning to the level of sacrifice and devotion of the people of Penang,” he said at the official opening of Fort Cornwallis after restoration works on the colonial monument. He said it is not necessarily erasing history but a fact that there is a different narrative behind the monuments left behind by the country’s former colonial masters.

items.title: Education groups Dong Zong and Jiao Zong decry PAS president Hadi Awang’s ‘pendatang’ remarks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Two of Malaysia’s largest Chinese education advocacy groups, Dong Zong and Jiao Zong, have issued a strong joint condemnation of PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang’s recent remarks labelling DAP supporters as “pendatang” (immigrants) and accusing some Malay Muslims of being “ungrateful” and “colluding” with others. In a joint statement released today, the duo—collectively known as Dong Jiao Zong—warned that such rhetoric undermines the national identity by defining citizenship along ethnic and religious lines, while distorting healthy political competition into inter-ethnic hostility. They said the remarks not only fail to strengthen national unity but also risk eroding the longstanding trust built among Malaysia’s diverse communities.

items.title: Former PM Najib undergoes coronary procedure; no stent needed, doctors confirm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Former Malaysian Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak is in stable condition and recovering after undergoing a coronary angiogram today, with doctors confirming that no further surgical intervention, such as balloon angioplasty or stent implantation, is required. According to a statement released by his legal counsel, Messrs Shafee & Co., the medical procedure was deemed necessary following a series of health evaluations over the past several weeks. The medical team had previously advised that there was an estimated 95% probability that Najib would require further intervention.

items.title: Sanusi warns of lawsuits, police reports over ‘distorted’ speech
items.summary: ALOR SETAR — Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor has warned that he will take legal action, including filing civil suits, against anyone found to be twisting his remarks for political gain, according to a report by Sinar Harian. Acccording to Sinar Harian , Sanusi told reporters he would lodge police reports against those he accused of distorting comments he made during a ceramah in Jempol, Negeri Sembilan, insisting his remarks were purely factual. Zahid said such remarks could stir unease among communities and suggested Sanusi focus instead on managing Kedah’s affairs ahead of polling day.

items.title: Police launch 16 probes into alleged election-related offences in Negeri Sembilan
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 25 — Negeri Sembilan police have received 16 reports and opened 11 investigation papers, including two opened yesterday, over alleged election-related offences in the state polls. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said one investigation paper opened yesterday was under Section 435 of the Penal Code for committing mischief by fire, resulting in the loss or damage of property. However, Alzafny said the security and public order situation throughout the election process remained good and under control.

items.title: Family, including baby, rescued from Tanjung Kling flash floods
items.summary: Melaka Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) public relations officer Mohd Hafidzatullah Rashid said seven firefighters from the Tangga Batu Fire and Rescue Station were deployed after the department received an emergency call at 9.47am. Meanwhile, Melaka Civil Defence Force (APM) director Lt Col (PA) Kamarulsyah Muslim said continuous heavy rain since 1 am caused several flood-prone areas in Melaka Tengah to be inundated. Kamarulsyah, who is also the State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) Secretariat spokesperson, said no temporary relief centre had been opened and no victims evacuated as of 10 am.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan cooperation with Perikatan does not bind BN, says Ahmad Maslan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Barisan Nasional’s cooperation with Perikatan Nasional in the Negeri Sembilan state election is only a political understanding and does not amount to a formal agreement, Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan said. According to Utusan Malaysia , Ahmad said there was no formal pact at the state level, leaving Umno and BN free to determine the strategies they considered best to remain relevant and win the election. “At the state level, there is no agreement.

items.title: Suspect arrested in Shah Alam for armed van heist attempt
items.summary: South Klang district police chief ACP Lim Jit Huey said the remand application for the local suspect in his 20s, was made at the Klang Court yesterday. “The court then granted the suspect a six-day remand starting yesterday until July 29,” he said via a Whatsapp message today. Earlier, Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M Kumar said the local suspect, in his 20s, was arrested in Shah Alam, Selangor at 11 am, July 23.

items.title: Melaka floods: Emergency shelters set up after relentless rain
items.summary: MELAKA, July 25 —Two temporary relief centres have been opened after heavy rain caused flooding in several areas in the Melaka Tengah and Jasin districts as of 3 pm today. Continuous heavy rain since early this morning has caused flooding in several areas in Melaka Tengah, namely Kampung Lereh, Peringgit, Kampung Bachang, Kampung Kolam Limbongan, Tengkera, Bukit Rambai, Tanjung Kling, Pengkalan Perigi and Kampung Berlian. In Jasin, the affected villages are Kampung Pulai, Kampung Serkam and Kampung Bukit Tembakau.

items.title: Calls for Malays to unite must go on, Sanusi’s speech taken out of context, says Annuar Musa
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Calls by leaders for Malays to unite, remain united and love their homeland must continue, Tan Sri Annuar Musa said today as he defended Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor over remarks that have drawn criticism for their racial tone. In a Facebook post, Annuar said Sanusi’s remarks had been taken out of context and denied that the PAS leader had intended to hurt the feelings of other ethnic communities in Malaysia. That is completely untrue.” he said.

items.title: Malaysia’s GNI per capita hits record high, ‘one step away’ from high-income nation, says HR minister
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, July 25 — Malaysia is now just one step away from achieving high-income nation status based on the World Bank's per capita income threshold, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said. He said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Malaysia's Gross National Income (GNI) per capita, measured using the World Bank Atlas method, has reached US$12,380 (about RM50,640), the highest level since independence. He said the country's economic size, measured by Gross Domestic Product (GDP), has also increased to US$472 billion, also the highest value since 1957.

items.title: ‘Malaysia is their home’: Azalina says Constitution protects rights of non-Malays alongside Malays
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said today said racial rhetoric had no place in the Negeri Sembilan election campaign, as she criticised remarks by Perikatan Nasional election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor. Azalina said such rhetoric could create the impression that Malaysians of Chinese and Indian descent had other homelands, while only Malays truly belonged in Malaysia. Malaysia is their homeland,” she said.

items.title: Aminuddin challenges BN manifesto, says Negeri Sembilan has already met RM30b investment target
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, July 25 — Negeri Sembilan’s economic performance under the Pakatan Harapan (PH) administration, particularly in terms of investment, has surpassed the target set by Barisan Nasional (BN) in its manifesto for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election, said state PH chairman Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun. He said BN’s target of RM30 billion in investments over five years did not reflect the state’s current economic performance, as Negeri Sembilan had achieved the target. The Negeri Sembilan BN manifesto, launched yesterday, targets RM30 billion in investments over five years if the coalition is given the mandate to govern the state.

items.title: PM Anwar condemns Kedah MB Sanusi’s divisive comments, calls for unity
items.summary: SEBERANG PERAI, July 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has strongly condemned Perikatan Nasional election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor over remarks suggesting that different ethnic groups in Malaysia could fall back on ancestral homelands outside the country. According to FMT, the Pakatan Harapan chairman said no leader should make statements that could offend other races, stressing that the Malaysian Chinese and Malaysian Indian communities are loyal citizens who respect the Federal Constitution. "The Malaysian Chinese and Malaysian Indian communities respect the constitution and are loyal citizens.

items.title: ‘There is no need to come to Negeri Sembilan’: Zahid tells Sanusi to focus on Kedah
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, July 25 — Deputy Prime Minister and Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has reminded Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor to steer clear of racial and religious sentiments during the Negeri Sembilan state election campaign. Astro Awani reported Zahid, Speaking to reporters after launching the “Madani Agriculture Commodity Programme” in Kuala Pilah today, said that if Sanusi truly wished to promote national unity, he should avoid touching on issues related to ethnicity, religion, culture or other racial backgrounds, as such remarks could stir unease among various communities. Zahid noted that Sanusi, who is also PAS’s election director for the state polls, may be accustomed to addressing Kedah’s electorate, but his style of speech may not sit well with the more diverse voters of Negeri Sembilan, where his words could be misinterpreted and cause unnecessary tension.

items.title: Rights body Suhakam voices concern over court ruling denying citizenship to children born out of wedlock
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — The Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) has expressed deep concern over a recent Court of Appeal decision that denies Malaysian citizenship to children born out of wedlock to Malaysian fathers and non-Malaysian mothers. While affirming full respect for judicial independence and acknowledging the court’s role in interpreting the Federal Constitution as it stands, Suhakam said the ruling exposes critical gaps in the country’s citizenship framework that could leave vulnerable children at risk of statelessness. “Every child has the right to acquire a nationality,” Suhakam said in a statement today, citing Article 7 of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC), to which Malaysia has been a signatory since 1995.

items.title: Johari: Malaysia given two years to tighten laws on forced labour imports under US trade deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Malaysia will have two years to introduce measures prohibiting imports of goods produced using forced labour under its trade agreement with the US, Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said today. He said the Human Resources Ministry had been informed of the changes required, including measures aimed at preventing Malaysian exports from incorporating imported materials or components produced through forced labour in third countries. Johari also addressed the US’ decision to impose a 10 per cent tariff on Malaysian imports following its investigation into countries that did not impose and effectively enforce restrictions on imports of goods produced using forced labour.

items.title: Anwar says decision on potential Formula One return to Malaysia will be announced tomorrow
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, July 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said developments regarding the possibility of Malaysia returning as a host for a Formula One (F1) race this year will be announced tomorrow. “The F1 matter will be announced on Sunday,” he said briefly when met by reporters after officially opening Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Agama Sheikh Tahir Jalaluddin and launching the Nuqaba programme here today. Yesterday, Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari said the ministry was actively discussing and assessing the possibility of Malaysia hosting the race to replace the Bahrain Grand Prix, which is scheduled to take place in October.

items.title: Take a hard look at yourselves before lecturing Malaysians on unity, Kasthuri tells Perikatan, PAS
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Perikatan Nasional and PAS should “walk the talk” on national unity before lecturing Malaysians about it, DAP’s Kasthuri Patto said today, as she criticised the use of racial rhetoric during the Negeri Sembilan election campaign. “Malaysians must reject politicians who manipulate and exploit race and religion for their own political survival,” she said in a statement. Kasthuri was responding to remarks by PN election director and Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor, as well as Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, which she said had brought racial considerations into the campaign.
